body:
## Parent

#121 — spec: Expected-set entry resolves its skill files

## What to build

The entry-level resolution status retires. Every consumer derives failure from the skill files it already reads, so one fact has one failure vocabulary and no code can consult a stale directory-level answer.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The entry no longer exposes a directory-level resolution status or its reason strings; failure is derived from the skill files the entry owns.
- [ ] Failure messages produced by the development flow, packaging, and validation keep naming the missing location and reason (no wording loss against the previous messages).
- [ ] The repo compiles and `cargo test --workspace` is green; no consumer reads the retired status (lint/clippy clean).
- [ ] Behavior is unchanged versus the previous ticket: development policy, packaging strictness, tarball layout, installed layout, lock format, and all entry-state verdicts are identical.
- [ ] The existing suites serve as the referee and stay green without relaxing any assertion.

## Blocked by

- #123 — Validation consumes enumerated skill files; codex status becomes a projection.
- #124 — Dev and pack consume skill files; release gate names every missing file.
- #125 — Toolkit-setup reads skill files instead of re-deriving the Expected set.
title: Retire the entry-level resolution status (contract)
